Sophia: heads-up — after the kernel-picker tweak from PR #4127 I'm seeing a consistent ~12% p99 token latency regression on our GQA+MQA workloads (seqlen=1024, batch=4) on A100. Ran the usual bench and attached a short log dump: ```
[bench] model=gqa-mqa-v2 seqlen=1024 batch=4 kv_layout=paged block=512
tokens/s: 210
p50: 18ms p95: 54ms p99: 112ms
kernel_picked: generic_attn_v2
expected_kernel: optimized_gqa_paged
cache_fragments: 43 pages
```
Anyone seen this pattern after the kernel selector change? :eyes:

Leo: yup, saw something similar in the nightly runs. My quick theory: the selector's architecture-aware scoring bumped the weight towards MQA-optimized kernels only if the KV-cache layout hits a compactness threshold; if paged layout is fragmented it prefers a general kernel. That fallback is much slower for long seqlens. Do we have the selector logs?

Sophia: here's the selector debug snippet I grabbed: ```
selector.score(optimized_gqa_paged)=0.38
selector.score(generic_attn_v2)=0.71
seqlen_bucket=1024
kv_compactness=0.42  # threshold 0.6
```

Arjun: interesting — kv_compactness < threshold explains the fallback. Two quick probes: (1) re-run bench with block_size=256 to see if fragmentation reduces, (2) enable KVCACHE_DEBUG to get page churn metrics. Also can we try forcing kernel via `KERNEL_OVERRIDE=optimized_gqa_paged` to confirm perf diff?

Claire: ran a micro-test locally. Forcing optimized_gqa_paged gave: p99 down to 96ms and tokens/s up to 238. So it's definitely a selector-fallback causing the hit. But if the kernel truly requires compact KV layout maybe it's unsafe to force globally.

infra-bot: [alert] perf-regression-detector: job 86321 flagged regression on gqa-mqa-v2 nightly (p99 +11%). See run: https://ci.internal/runs/86321

Kenneth: can we adjust the selector to consider historical frag metrics per instance instead of current compactness only? Maybe a hysteresis so temporary fragmentation doesn't flip picks. Also check if the recent allocator change in #4109 increased page churn.

Leo: agree on hysteresis. Short-term mitigation: pin the kernel selection policy for the Dedicated pool to prefer optimized_gqa_paged for model families matching gqa-mqa-v* when seqlen >= 512. That buys us perf while we tune allocator. I can open a small config PR.

Sophia: action items: (1) Arjun run KVCACHE_DEBUG and block_size sweep (256/512/1024) and drop results here, (2) Leo open policy pin PR and add a canary rollout to 10% Dedicated, (3) Claire confirm stability of forced kernel across seqlen distribution. I'll also revert the selector change in a canary if we see broader impact.

Arjun: started runs — command I'm using: ```
./bench --model gqa-mqa-v2 --seqlen 1024 --batch 4 --kv-layout paged --block 256 --env KVCACHE_DEBUG=1 --env KERNEL_OVERRIDE=""
```
will post logs in ~20m.

Claire: quick note — when forcing optimized_gqa_paged I saw a small memory spike (~4%) but no OOM on A100. Good sign. :+1:

Sophia: thanks all. tagging @Kenneth to keep an eye on allocator PR #4109. we'll regroup after Arjun posts logs. :memo:
